# Module `agents`

agents - lightweight isolated message-passing units.

An agent is a unit of concurrency that owns a mailbox (an unbounded Int
channel) and runs a behavior loop on its own worker thread: it blocks on recv
and hands each message to the behavior closure. Only messages cross the
boundary -- the agent's internal state stays private to its behavior. The
handle is an Int (a runtime table index).

Usage:
  import agents

  counter = agent_start(|v<Int>| -> {
      println("got " + v.to_string())
  })

  ok = agent_send(counter, 42)   // 1
  agent_send(counter, 43)
  agent_close(counter)           // drain then stop (lossless)
  agent_free(counter)            // wait for the worker and reclaim

A behavior loop exits once the mailbox is closed and drained, so shutdown is
cooperative and loses no buffered messages. agent_free closes the mailbox if
it was never closed, then waits for the worker before reclaiming.

```
agent_close(a<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Gracefully stop: close the mailbox; the agent drains buffered messages then
stops. Returns 1, or -1 on a bad handle.

<a id="sym-agent_dead_letter"></a>
### `agent_dead_letter` · fn

```
agent_dead_letter(a<Int>, ch<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Register an int-slot reply channel as a dead-letter: on failure the runtime
sends the agent's own handle into `ch` so a supervisor can react, then query
agent_status / agent_error for details. Returns 1, or -1 on a bad handle.

<a id="sym-agent_mailbox"></a>
### `agent_mailbox` · fn

```
agent_mailbox(a<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Expose the agent's underlying mailbox channel handle (scalar agents only).
Int/Bool/Float agents ride an int-slot channel, so the returned handle can be
passed to chan_select (alongside reply channels) to compose agents into
fan-in/fan-out and watch multiple agents' readiness from one place. String
agents use a separate mailbox type and return -1 here. The handle aliases the
agent's mailbox: it is freed by agent_free and must not be closed/freed by the
caller; treat it as read-only (select/len observation), not a side channel for
consuming messages (that is the behavior's own recv loop).
